## Testing for Kidney Disease

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Testing for kidney disease
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
testing_kidney <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Biomedical_KidneyTest.csv")

# Data wrangling
testing_kidney <- testing_kidney %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(yes_has_been_tested_in_last_3_years_n:no_has_not_been_tested_in_last_3_years_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(test_n   = yes_has_been_tested_in_last_3_years_n,
                notest_n = no_has_not_been_tested_in_last_3_years_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(test_n:notest_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("test"),
                starts_with("notest"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to      = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "test"     = "Yes",
                                              "notest"   = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 18% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they had been tested for kidney disease during the three years prior to the survey. This equates to approximately 6,900 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Males were more likely to have been tested for kidney disease than females (24% vs. 12%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data for this topic were collected from all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- `r note_aboriginality_natsihs`
:::

## Kidney Disease

### Self-Reported Kidney Disease

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kidney disease, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
kidney_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Health_Kidney_LGA.csv",
                                variable = "kidney") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(kidney != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
kidney_lga <- kidney_lga %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(kidney = dplyr::case_when(
    kidney == "Has kidney disease" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = kidney,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kidney disease, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
kidney_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Health_Kidney_AgeSex.csv",
                                      variable = "kidney") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(kidney != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
kidney_agesex <- kidney_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(kidney = dplyr::case_when(
    kidney == "Has kidney disease" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>%  
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = kidney,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 1.2% (n = 141) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have kidney disease. This was higher than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (0.9%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have kidney disease ranged from 26 (Darebin LGA) to 0 (Manningham and Yarra LGAs).

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have kidney disease and the expected number if the proportion was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for Darebin and Hume LGAs.

- The percentage of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have kidney disease ranged from 2.0% (Whitehorse LGA) to 0.0% (Manningham and Yarra LGAs).

- The number of people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have kidney disease was highest for people aged 60-69 years for both males and females, and the percentage of people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have kidney disease increased with increasing age. Note that these data should be interpreted with caution due to small numbers and a high proportion of people being excluded due to missing data on age and/or sex.

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultation during the development of this report, the often late diagnosis of kidney disease was discussed as an issue affecting Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- In addition, the term ‘kidney disease’ may have been misunderstood and not responded to accurately in the Census.

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data for this topic were collected from all people completing the ABS Census 2021.

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- `r note_aboriginality_census`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- People were classified as having kidney disease if they selected *Kidney disease*.
:::

  - Arthritis
  - Asthma
  - Cancer (including remission)
  - Dementia (including Alzheimer's)  
  - Diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes)
  - Heart disease (including heart attack or angina)
  - Kidney disease
  - Lung condition (including COPD or emphysema)
  - Mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)
  - Stroke
  - Any other long-term health condition(s)
  - No long-term health condition

:::

### Hospital Admissions for Chronic Kidney Disease

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - chronic kidney disease
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_kidney <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_principal_diag",
                                              column_select = "admissions_for_chronic_kidney_disease_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_kidney <- hospital_kidney %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Social Health Atlas of Australia](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases), compiled from the [Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED)](https://www.health.vic.gov.au/data-reporting/victorian-admitted-episodes-dataset).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 293 hospital admissions for chronic kidney disease for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for chronic kidney disease for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 55 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 5 (Whitehorse and Yarra Ranges IAREs).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for chronic kidney disease for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 395 per 100,000 population (Maroondah IARE) to 58 per 100,000 population (Yarra Ranges IARE).

- 6 of the 8 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area with data available for reporting had an age-standardised admission rate for chronic kidney disease above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Maroondah, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Melbourne East, Whitehorse, Moreland/Broadmeadows, and Melbourne/Port Phillip IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for chronic kidney disease were defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - Malaria: B52.0
  - Haemolytic anaemias: D59.3
  - Diabetes mellitus: E10.2, E11.2, E13.2, E14.2
  - Neuropathic heredofamilial amyloidosis: E85.1
  - Hypertensive diseases: I12, I13, I15.0, I15.1
  - Glomerular diseases: N00, N01, N02, N03, N04, N05, N06, N07, N08
  - Renal tubulo-interstitial diseases: N11, N12, N14, N15
  - Renal failure: N18, N19
  - Other disorders of kidney and ureter: N25, N26, N27, N28
  - Other diseases of urinary system: N39.1, N39.2
  - Congenital malformations of the urinary system: Q60, Q61, Q62, Q63
  - Complications of surgical and medical care: T82.4, T86.1
  - Care involving dialysis: Z49.0 

:::

### Hospital Admissions for Dialysis

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - dialysis
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_dialysis <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_same_day_renal",
                                                column_select = "same_day_admissions_for_dialysis_for_kidney_disease_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_dialysis <- hospital_dialysis %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Social Health Atlas of Australia](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases), compiled from the [Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED)](https://www.health.vic.gov.au/data-reporting/victorian-admitted-episodes-dataset).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 9,786 same day hospital admissions for dialysis for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of same day hospital admissions for dialysis for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 1,652 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 91 (Yarra Ranges IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of same day hospital admissions for dialysis for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 13,438 per 100,000 population (Melbourne/Port Phillip IARE) to 990 per 100,000 population (Yarra Ranges IARE).

- 3 of the 7 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area with data available for reporting had an age-standardised same day admission rate for dialysis above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Melbourne/Port Phillip, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, and Craigieburn/Sunbury IAREs).
